chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who swore to her husband by manumission and offering (of a sacrificial animal) that she would never marry after him, then it became pleasing to her to marry. He said: 'She sells her slave (to free herself from the oath), for I fear Satan upon her, and there is no obligation upon her in the right (of the husband), and if she wishes to offer a sacrifice, she may do so.'

key_terms.الْعَتَاقِ: Manumission of a slave (expiation for oaths)
key_terms.اَلشَّيْطَانَ: Satan (feared to cause hardship due to the oath)
key_terms.تَبِيعُ مَمْلُوكَهَا: She sells her slave (to free them as expiation)
key_terms.فِي اَلْحَقِّ: In the right/obligation (referring to the husband's claim)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a woman's oath not to remarry after her husband's death in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the expiation (kaffarah) for a woman’s vow of continence (not remarrying) upon her husband's death, prescribing the freeing of a slave as the primary remedy to ward off Satan's influence. He distinguishes this personal vow from the husband's rights, noting it is not obligatory upon him, while allowing voluntary offering of a sacrifice (hady) if she chooses. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on individual accountability in vows and the practical mechanism of manumission as a primary form of expiation.
